messages.subject_clean: One failing test in latest version of PKI
messages.body_plain:
Hi Simon,

when trying to build PKI for Debian I stumbled upon the following
error of the test suite:

LC_ALL=C.UTF-8 R --no-save < tests/test.R

    > ## on some systems using abs paths can break 100 byte limit
    > ## so we must do this in the tempdir
    > wd <- getwd()
    > td <- tempdir()
    > setwd(td)
    > tar(fn, basename(tmpfn), "none")
    > PKI.sign.tar(fn, key)
    Error: (converted from warning) input string '�7zXZ' cannot be translated to UTF-8, is it valid in 'ANSI_X3.4-1968'?
    Execution halted

Do you have any idea how to fix this?

Kind regards

      Andreas.

-- 
http://fam-tille.de

messages.subject_clean: One failing test in latest version of PKI
messages.body_plain:
Andreas,

thanks for alerting me about the OpenSSL issue - this is now fixed upstream:
https://github.com/s-u/PKI/commit/af3cbcafa13322d170e8ef993b919f57decf45e9

As for other error you see - that comes from
rawToChar(magic[1:5]) == "\xfd7zXZ"
I don't have any details on your setup (I cannot replicate) so I don't know why it happens (maybe that notorious C.UTF-8 locale again?), but should be easily fixed by avoiding strings.
https://github.com/s-u/PKI/issues/27
Please let me know if the latest version works for you.
https://rforge.net/PKI/snapshot/PKI_0.1-11.tar.gz

Cheers,
Simon

the OpenSSL issue is worth a soonish release in any case so I'd be happy
if you push the current status to CRAN and I try to build what I can
find there.

Kind regards

    Andreas.

messages.subject: qqconf fails to build on !x86
messages.body_plain:
Hi Eric,

qqconf[1] fails to build on !x86 with gcc-12 compiler due to
"mm_malloc.h" not being present on all architectures.

I have a small patch to fix this, which you can find here[2]
Could you please consider to apply it upstream?

[1]: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/qqconf/index.html
[2]: https://salsa.debian.org/r-pkg-team/r-cran-qqconf/-/blob/master/debian/patches/fix-compilation-on-non-x86.patch

Regards,
Nilesh

messages.subject: bslib and rmarkdown update
messages.body_plain:
Andreas and others,

The new version of rmarkdown really needs r-cran-bslib
which uses some google fonts[details here], and might trigger rejects from FTP masters.

I suggest to strip these off for now, and upload to new. We need markdown soonish.
Some functionality might be broken, but atleast we will have it working.

What do you think?

[details here]: https://lists.debian.org/debian-r/2022/02/msg00016.html

Regards,
Nilesh
